title: How venture works: what Garry Tan looks for in VCs and founders at Initialized
summary: Garry Tan explains how a VC fund exists to return money to limited partners, why brand and early access matter, and what makes a good investor. He stresses technical builders, contrarian belief, and being fair, direct and honest, then announces Initialized is hiring a principal and a partner.

principles.text: Back technical, product and design-oriented founders; the ones who can build it usually do.
principles.quote: at initialized we have a strong preference for technical product and design-oriented founders because those are the builders who have actually changed the world the ones who can build it usually do.

principles.text: Founder drive and persistence are powerful signals; a builder who can make you believe can make everyone believe.
principles.quote: if you have a builder who can make you believe then they can make everyone believe and that's how you can build something truly great

principles.text: Avoid paint-by-numbers, buzzword-combo startup ideas; look for independent first-principles thinkers.
principles.quote: we're looking for people who are independent thinkers who think from first principles and if you're that kind of person you're gonna see paint by numbers right away

principles.text: Test for contrarian insight by asking what someone believes that nobody else believes.
principles.quote: the best way to figure out if someone sitting across from you has secret knowledge at all is to ask them what do you believe that nobody else believes

principles.text: Being fair, direct and honest wins in venture's long iterative game; bad actors suffer adverse selection.
principles.quote: the best founders can choose anyone and they will choose those who are most trustworthy first being a bad actor is adverse selection in an iterative infinite game like venture capital

principles.text: When a startup struggles, investors should find the root cause rather than squeeze or micromanage founders.
principles.quote: instead of making founders feel like employees the right thing to do is help identify the root cause
